solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charlie gets out of bed for emergencies

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
someone getting out of bed rises

explanation.surface: Charlie only gets up when something urgent happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are moments of acute danger or difficulty, which is what emergencies are.

clue.text: Ray may do this about French parliamentary bill

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
a bill passed by parliament becomes an act

explanation.surface: Ray may revise a French parliamentary bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is a ray of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A light ray bends when passing into a new medium, which is how refraction works.

clue.text: Bush finds credit in reserve

indicators.note: in puts the credit abbreviation inside the reserve's letters

parts.note: a sub, short for substitute, is a reserve player

explanation.surface: A president named Bush finds some credit held in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the US president; it is low shrubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub is low, stunted vegetation, brushwood and shrubs.

clue.text: Vibration caused by Roller in good condition?

parts.note: sound means healthy or in good condition
a roller is a long wave breaking on a shore

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce in fine shape still produces vibration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' hints at a Rolls-Royce car; it is a big sea wave.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic energy travels as an oscillation of pressure through air, a form of vibration.

clue.text: Quiet lake in Ireland — before journalist turned up!

indicators.note: before places the lake ahead of the journalist in the answer

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an Irish lake is a lough
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A quiet Irish lakeside is disturbed when a reporter arrives unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as 'arrived', but here it is soil turned over by a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughed land has had its soil turned up by the blade.

clue.text: House sitters look mature

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: People minding a house appear grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the House of Lords, whose members sit there.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of lords collectively seated in the upper chamber of Parliament.

clue.text: Poem about theatre in Greece

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A poem written about a theatre in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a roofed building for musical performances bore this name.

clue.text: Fashion model glad to get top award

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of model glad are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model is pleased to win the top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: First place in Olympic events earns a prize of gold, the highest honour.

clue.text: Being serious, set out to support merit

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of set are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone set out in earnest to back merit.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is sincere and grave, never frivolous.

clue.text: One's prediction unfortunately not true in case of lumberjack

indicators.note: the lumberjack's word forms a case holding the other letters

parts.note: a lumberjack fells trees, so is a feller

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the words not true have gone awry and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prophecy about a lumberjack turns out to be false.
explanation.walkthrough: A lumberjack fells trees, hence the case word; 'One's prediction' stands for the person who makes predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person makes predictions about clients' futures for a living.

clue.text: Nation seeing a married chap taken in by agents

indicators.note: taken in by means the first pieces sit inside the agents' letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents
BOD is British slang for a person, a chap

explanation.surface: A married man is detained by intelligence agents abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country in Southeast Asia, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Cardinal's song?

definitions.meaning: a cardinal is a counting ... such as one, two, three
a song or piece in a show is called a ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is the cardinal number of arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a counting quantity and a performed piece of music share this word.

clue.text: Sailor's back on street before A levels

indicators.note: back tells us the sailor's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor returns to his street before sitting his A level exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAR into RAT; 'A levels' looks like the exams but the A is a letter and 'levels' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or society, stacked one above another like levels.

clue.text: Panicked at Nixon welcoming Italian remedy

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece holds another
panicked suggests frantic disorder, so the letters of at Nixon are jumbled

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Panicked Nixon is welcomed by an Italian offering a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panicked' signals the anagram of AT NIXON; 'welcoming' tells you the Italian abbreviation goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antitoxin counteracts a poison, a remedy against it.

clue.text: Speed up progress of divorcee with exercise and new diet

parts.note: a former spouse is an ex
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of diet are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A divorcee tries to hasten her progress with a workout and a new diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite a matter is to make it move faster, hurrying it along.

clue.text: Person who buys almost perfect hunter

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for perfect is missing

parts.note: pure means flawless, perfect
a hunter chases prey, so is a chaser

explanation.surface: A customer buys a nearly flawless hunting horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser is a buyer, someone who acquires goods for money.

clue.text: Lock on Barbarian's woman after game

indicators.note: in an across clue, the lock placed on the barbarian comes after it

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders of the Roman Empire
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A barbarian's woman follows the game.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a female hunter, a woman pursuing quarry.

clue.text: A foreign male in maintained environment gets untidy

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: in puts the male abbreviation inside the word for maintained

parts.note: something maintained is kept

explanation.surface: A foreign man in a well kept setting looks scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt hair or clothes are dishevelled, messy and neglected.

clue.text: Colour of small runabout perhaps on lease

parts.note: a runabout is a small car, an example of one
to let is to lease out property

explanation.surface: Asking the colour of a small car one is renting.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red, a particular colour.

clue.text: Slither around with no time for enjoyment

indicators.note: around signals the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
with no means a letter is taken out of the word slither

explanation.surface: A snake slithers about without any pleasure in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops T from SLITHER to leave SLIHER, which 'around' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish is gusto or keen pleasure taken in something.

clue.text: Deception left crew under six, nine having gone

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the left-and-crew pieces below what remains of six
nine in Roman numerals is IX, and those letters are taken away from six

parts.note: six taken as written
a rowing eight is a crew of oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing team below a certain number is hiding some trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: IX is nine in Roman numerals; an eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is cunning or trickery, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Sportsperson making fish run?

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish related to rays
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete wonders what makes a fish swim off.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater competes on ice or wheels, a type of athlete.

clue.text: Travelled west of Oregon for cowboy show

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle
O is a short abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

explanation.surface: Someone rode out west of Oregon to see a cowboy display.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'west of' puts RODE above O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show where cowboys ride broncos and rope cattle.

clue.text: Gets bill, with robbers losing head

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the robbers' word is dropped

parts.note: robbers are thieves

explanation.surface: Someone receives an invoice as the gang of robbers loses its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to attain or obtain it.

clue.text: Force out and achieve victory, to a limited extent

indicators.note: to a limited extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Win a limited triumph by driving the opposition out.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from property, forcing them out.

clue.text: Something both good and bad that could lead to glibness!

parts.note: the letters of the second word, when mixed up, give glibness, so the answer is an instruction producing the clue word

explanation.surface: Something with pros and cons might make a person glib.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: BLESSING with 'mixed' as an anagram signal gives GLIBNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a thing with advantages and disadvantages together.

clue.text: Be proud, though dismissed by platform

parts.note: a stand is a raised platform
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Someone stays dignified despite being sacked from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proud' is meant in its sense of projecting, sticking out from a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proud of a surface protrudes, so it is prominent or projecting.

clue.text: Go round, consumed by rubbish

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: Someone walks round, swallowed up by heaps of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, revolving.
